predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: the Britons of Alt Clut round Dumbarton Rock and the Clyde

successors.name: Kingdom of Alba
successors.text: the Clyde, Lanarkshire and Dumfriesshire: Cliopatria's Alba shape of 1034 is the 1033 Alba shape plus exactly this shape

ledger.x: 642-644: the Britons of Alt Clut stand as their own kingdom.
750: Cliopatria hands the northern salient to Dal Riata's shape.

c. 900: Strathclyde takes Cumbria. 'Around the year 900, after the power of Northumbria was destroyed by Viking incursions and settlement, large areas west of the Pennines fell without apparent warfare under the control of the Brittonic Kingdom of Strathclyde'; the Strathclyde page puts the Keswick-area…
12 July 927: Owain of Strathclyde accepts Æthelstan's overlordship at Eamont.
937: Strathclyde joins the invasion of England.

wars.name: Pictish and Northumbrian war on Alt Clut
wars.outcome: Mocetauc 750 (Talorgan, brother of Oengus, killed); Kyle taken by Eadberht in 750; Oengus and Eadberht take terms from the Britons at Dumbarton on 1 August 756, the combined army perishing on the tenth.

wars.name: Viking siege of Dumbarton
wars.outcome: Amlaib Conung and Imar besiege Dumbarton for 'some four months'; the capital seems to move to Govan afterwards.

wars.name: Brunanburh campaign
wars.outcome: Owain of Strathclyde joins Constantine and the Vikings in invading England in 937 and is beaten at Brunanburh; no change of frontier on the pages.

wars.name: Edmund's invasion of Strathclyde
wars.outcome: Edmund ravages Strathclyde and 'gave the kingdom to King Malcolm I of Scotland'; 'Dyfnwal soon recovered it'.

wars.name: Battle of Carham
wars.outcome: Scottish victory over Uhtred; 'Lothian and the region north of Berwick integrated fully into Scotland' (infobox).
